{{Quote|Can you not feel the ''potency'' of this place?|Freedon Nadd|audio=NaddPotency.flac|<ref name="DLotSaudio">[[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' audio drama]]</ref>}}
The '''Valley of the Dark Lords''', originally known as the '''Valley of the Sleeping Kings''', was a valley and [[Burial/Legends|burial]] ground of the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. Originally constructed by the [[Sith (species)/Legends|planet's natives]] as a burial ground for their kings; the [[Exiles]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] who came to be known as the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] added their own tombs to the valley. Along with several prominent tombs, the valley was home to the ancient [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Great Temple (Korriban)|Great Temple]] and the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]], which loomed over the valley for several millennia.

==History==
===Valley of the Sleeping Kings===
{{Quote|Be careful. Dark energy fills these ruins... and even the fallen Sith live still.|[[Kreia]]|<ref name="KOTORII" />}}
Built long before the arrival of the [[Exiles]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] in [[6900 BBY]], the Valley of the Sleeping Kings was located in a sheer rock valley on the planet [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], where the dust contained the remnants of a thousand kings long dead. Smoothing the walls of the valley and fashioning giant statues of [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] shape, the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] of Korriban long [[Burial/Legends|buried]] their rulers in the stone tombs deep within the walls of the valley. At the conclusion of the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]], a war fought far from Korriban, the [[Exiles]] as they were called after being banished from the space controlled by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], landed on the dusty world. Numbering only eleven, the Exiles were welcomed as gods by the primitive Sith and eventually took up the titles of [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lords of the Sith]]. Founding the first [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] after [[Death/Legends|killing]] [[King/Legends|King]] [[Hakagram Graush]], [[Ajunta Pall]] took control of the Empire and was worshiped and feared by his followers.<ref name="BOS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

Following the death of Lord Pall, a [[Tomb of Ajunta Pall|mausoleum]] was erected in the center of the valley, separate from the line of kings which were housed in the walls of the ancient edifices. Marked with runes and ancient spells, the tomb housed Pall's body against the destructive heat of the outside world, preserving the bones and [[Force ghost/Legends|spirit]] of the ancient Sith Lord. Eventually, Lord [[Tulak Hord]] came to control the Empire, ruling from Korriban and known as the Lord of Hate. The Sith Lord placed his loyal servant [[Khem Val]] in stasis within an old tomb within the walls of the valley before he himself was [[Tomb of Tulak Hord|laid to rest there]]. Over time, the valley would see the addition of a [[Tomb of Marka Ragnos|tomb]] for Lord [[Marka Ragnos]], and an [[Tomb of Naga Sadow|ancient tomb]] containing a [[Star Map]] of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] was converted to hold the remains of [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]], though he never was laid to rest within.<ref name="TOR" />

[[File:ValleyOfTheDarkLords-SaL.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The valley circa [[3993 BBY]]]]

Following Ragnos' reign, the Sith Empire was fractured during a [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|costly war]] of vengeance against the Galactic Republic and the Jedi Order under Naga Sadow, the new Dark Lord. After Sadow fled to [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], a [[Post–Great Hyperspace War counterinvasion|counterinvasion]] was sanctioned by [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Pultimo]]<ref name="TORE" /><ref name="TEA" /><ref name="TEGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> and the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] attacked the valley. As the valley burned, the Sith fled to [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]] and prepared to return and seek revenge on their persecutors.<ref name="TORE" />

===The Brotherhood of the Sith===
Over the ensuing centuries, the valley was visited by grave robbers and treasure seekers who infiltrated the defenses of the tombs and stole priceless artifacts from the ancient Sith Empire's old stronghold. In [[3997 BBY]], [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] visited the [[Great Temple (Korriban)|Great Temple]] in his quest for Sith knowledge<ref name="dlots2">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 2]]</ref><ref name="TOTJ3" /> and then established a [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith academy]] next to the valley.<ref name="TEA" /> After Kun's downfall, his disciples kept the academy running.<ref name="sal">{{Tales|23|Shadows and Light}}</ref>

===The reign of Revan===
{{Quote|It seems quiet - just the wind... but deep beneath the surface, you can feel the pain of what took place here. There is great power in this place - for those who can hear its call. |[[Visas Marr]]|<ref name="KOTORII" />}}
In [[3959 BBY]], the former [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] turned [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Revan/Legends|Darth Revan]] entered the valley with his apprentice [[Darth Malak]] with their own [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Imperial host]]. Taking control of the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]]<ref name="KOTORCG">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> at the valley's back wall, the Sith began churning out [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] to fight in Revan's [[Jedi Civil War|war]] with the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic. When Revan was captured and redeemed by the Jedi, he was dispatched to Korriban in the guise of a [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] and infiltrated the academy in order to gain access to the tombs. Retrieving artifacts such as [[Sword of Ajunta Pall|Ajunta Pall's blade]] and the [[Tulak Hord's holocron|holocron of Tulak Hord]], Revan escaped the valley undetected.<ref name="KOTOR" />

[[File:Ebonvalley.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The ''[[Ebon Hawk]]'' lands in the Valley of the Dark Lords in [[3951 BBY]].]]

When the war came to an end with the death of Darth Malak, the academy was abandoned as the remaining Sith fled [[Sith Civil War|infighting]]. During the [[First Jedi Purge]], the [[Sith Triumvirate]] did not return to Korriban. Jedi Knight [[Meetra Surik]] traveled to the valley in search of Master [[Lonna Vash]]. Most of the tombs' entrances had caved in with the exception of the [[Tomb of Ludo Kressh|burial chamber]] of [[Ludo Kressh]], which remained largely unscathed.<ref name="KOTORII" />

===Return of the Sith Empire===
In [[3681 BBY]], after centuries in hiding, the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] returned in force to the galaxy and retook Korriban. In a stunning [[Battle of Korriban|orbital battle]], [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Vindican|Vindican]] conquered the world and wiped out the Republic's forces stationed at the [[Korriban's orbital security station|orbital facility]] charged with maintaining the planetary quarantine. As the Sith resettled the valley, the academy reopened and began producing Sith to fight the Republic and the Jedi in the ongoing [[Great Galactic War]]. When the [[Treaty of Coruscant]] was signed, a [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] ensued, and life on Korriban thrived as a training ground for the Sith and their [[Imperial soldier|soldiers]] alike.<ref name="TOR" />

[[File:KorribanGGW.png|thumb|left|250px|The Academy of Korriban]]

As the Cold War went on, the excavation of the valley progressed significantly under the guidance of [[Darth Thanaton]]. To the dismay of the Sith, a great number of [[K'lor'slug/Legends|k'lor'slugs]] had infested the valley and the lower tombs while [[Tuk'ata/Legends|tuk'ata]] protected the higher tombs from grave robbers, vestiges of old [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemical experimentation]]. The Academy and the Sith flourished for many years and throughout the [[Galactic War]] until the Empire's final defeat.<ref name="TOR" /> After the Sith were vanquished, the Jedi pillaged the valley and confiscated or destroyed all remaining relics they could find, bringing an end to much of the work accomplished by the Sith over the past three millennia.<ref name="POD" />

===The Brotherhood of Darkness===
As the [[New Sith]] Empire and the Republic [[New Sith Wars|battled ceaselessly]] for generations, the Sith remained separated from their origin world. Under the leadership of Sith Lord [[Skere Kaan]] and his reorganized [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]], the Sith [[Battle of Korriban (New Sith Wars)|took back]] Korriban in a stunning victory which left all Jedi and Republic soldiers on the battlefield dead. They found the valley desolate, having been largely ignored by generations of Sith; dark siders during the [[New Sith Wars]] seldom if ever visited the site as centuries of looting and conflict had largely destroyed anything of value. Under Kaan's leadership and the works of Lords [[Qordis]] and [[Kopecz]], Korriban was reinvigorated and the Academy reopened in a new building in [[1006 BBY]]. As the Sith flocked to Korriban and sent hundreds through the academy system, the valley remained largely abandoned, as the Masters believed it to be empty of all relics or secrets that could aid in the war effort.<ref name="POD" />

Nonetheless, a headstrong and powerful student named [[Darth Bane/Legends|Bane]] defied his masters and made the treacherous journey from the city of [[Dreshdae]] in hopes of uncovering ancient secrets. While on Korriban, Bane felt the gentle hum of the dark side that permeated the air and hoped it would intensify within the valley itself. Instead, Bane found that the air within the valley had grown still, and that the dark side had retreated from the ancient edifices long ago. Searching the valley for knowledge for thirteen days, Bane concluded that the wealth of the valley had long ago disappeared and abandoned it forever.<ref name="POD" />

===A sleeping menace===
{{Quote|Of course there are tombs in the Valley of the Dark Lords, but they have been plundered and now draw only tourists.|[[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]]|<ref name="DP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>}}
[[File:JKAlevelshot_kor2.png|thumb|right|200px|The Valley of the Dark Lords, c. [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]]]]
Since the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformations]] of the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], Korriban and the valley remained largely depopulated and seldom visited as the Jedi Order entered a [[Golden Age of the Old Republic|golden age]] of peace. While the remaining Sith were deep in hiding, [[Force Adept]]s interested in the dark side sought out the treasures hidden deep in Korriban's tombs; most visitors were lost in the valley forever, never to emerge.

But in [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]], a team of Jedi Knights and their [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]], headed by [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], entered the Valley of the Dark Lords, after having visited the Sith Academy, while on a [[Mission to Korriban (23 BBY)|mission]] to track down the galactic criminals [[Granta Omega]] and [[Jenna Zan Arbor]].<ref name=":0">''[[Jedi Quest: The Final Showdown]]''</ref> Upon entering the Academy's ancient ruins, Kenobi felt a distinct Sith presence—the dark shape of a Sith Lord. Though he did not realize it at the time, this later proved to have been [[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus]] (the Sith alter ego of Count Dooku), who was there on Korriban to rendezvous with Omega and Zan Arbor. The two criminals were seeking to strike an alliance of power with the galaxy's re-emergent Sith. As 18-year-old [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] looked out towards the grayness of the Valley of the Dark Lords from the Academy's landing platform, he felt the beating heart of the Sith Lord reaching out, calling to him—its pull was powerful, insistent, irresistible. The Jedi team, aboard a borrowed [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]] [[Koro-1 airspeeder|airspeeder]] (their [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|Republic cruisers]] having just exploded from sabotage), were, within the hour and before dusk, pursuing Omega and Zan Arbor to the Valley of the Dark Lords. There, they at last confronted the long-sought criminals in a final showdown, after having spent years tracking them down (for both Omega and Zan Arbor had somehow always managed, at the last moment, to escape the Jedi's reach).<ref name="Jedi Quest: The Trail of the Jedi">''[[Jedi Quest: The Trail of the Jedi]]''</ref><ref name="Jedi Quest: The Master of Disguise">''[[Jedi Quest: The Master of Disguise]]''</ref><ref name="Jedi Quest: The Shadow Trap">''[[Jedi Quest: The Shadow Trap]]''</ref><ref name="Jedi Quest: The Moment of Truth">''[[Jedi Quest: The Moment of Truth]]''</ref><ref name="Jedi Quest: The Changing of the Guard">''[[Jedi Quest: The Changing of the Guard]]''</ref><ref name="Jedi Quest: The False Peace">''[[Jedi Quest: The False Peace]]''</ref>

As the Jedi entered the valley proper, a [[Waves of darkness|dark wave]] hit them, causing them to stop—it fractured [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] they felt around them, tearing at it. The [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] was more concentrated than they'd expected it to be. The Sith tombs that inhabited the valley were designed to amplify [[dark energy]], and the Jedi could feel that physical presence press against their chests, instinctively making them reach for their [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] hilts. It was only after battling their way through ten tuk'ata beasts—those fabled Sith sentinels of terror—that they were able to proceed down the mausoleum-lined valley. The dark energies of the dead Sith Lords, having awoken to the Jedi presence, poured from the mausoleums, and the Jedi could taste their anger, cruelty, and pain. Obi-Wan Kenobi reached out with the Force and detected the mausoleum that Omega and Zan Arbor had gone into for their secret meeting with the Sith Lord. Once the Jedi had entered, the Dark Lords' whispers grew louder as they advanced. Rising from their crumbling tombs, the Sith Lords approached the Jedi, their shroud-rags falling away, their mouths gaping, their hands grasping, their whispers taunting the intruders. But then the specters merely disintegrated onto the Jedi with foul smells and tastes. The dark side of the Force felt as thick as a curtain, however, and slowed the Jedi's movement, as if it were a physical presence.<ref name=":0" />

The Jedi soon encountered [[dark energy trap]]s, concentrations of dark-side power that appeared as faint shimmers of purple in the air: these, of course, could immobilize a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] being for a time, but the Jedi were able to stay clear of them with Kenobi's advance warning. But suddenly, Omega appeared from behind a tomb, arrogant, cruel, sure of himself, laughing in vengeful derision. Zan Arbor was there, too, in the shadows. Kenobi held their gaze, with no desire to speak, though without anger. He simply wouldn't respond to Omega's taunts—but rather held fast to his grim commitment to finish this unsavory but necessary task. It was time to rid the galaxy of this heinous scourge. Having first to battle through a platoon of [[Korriban zombie]]s, released by the Sith Lord in the wings, to stall them, the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] broke through to advance on the criminals. But Omega and Zan Arbor had slipped away into the darkness around the back of the tombs and appeared again from behind—as did the Sith Lord, who stood waiting for them at the tombs' entrance: the three villains were about to escape through the mausoleum's front door. Tragedy struck, however, when Padawan [[Darra Thel-Tanis]] was killed by Omega (due to Padawan [[Tru Veld/Legends|Tru Veld's]] faulty lightsaber that Padawan [[Ferus Olin]] was using as backup cover to his fellow Jedi). While Zan Arbor eventually fled behind the protective barrier of the Sith Lord's blue [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]], Omega stood firm, refusing to give up this chance to avenge himself of what he erroneously perceived to be his father [[Xanatos]]' death at the hands of the Jedi.<ref name="Jedi Apprentice: The Day of Reckoning">''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Day of Reckoning]]''</ref><ref name=":0" />

Although Omega temporarily blinded him by the flash of a [[Lumablast Rocket]], Kenobi, recovering, stood to face his longtime nemesis in a final showdown. Wildly parrying [[E-Web heavy repeating blaster/Legends|E-Web heavy repeating blaster]] fire and [[Wrist rocket/Legends|wrist rockets]], Kenobi drove through the distraction to achieve his somber aim. But because Omega was not aware of his own weapon's potential defects, as Obi-Wan surely was, he was utterly unprepared for the grim consequences of such ignorance: that the weapon, overburdened, could turn against itself by overloading, shutting down, and back-blasting—which it did. The resultant explosion slammed Omega into a tomb wall, breaking his body. But the ever-resilient arch-villain, refusing yet to surrender to death, lurched forward one last time with blaster fire, swearing to Obi-Wan that because the Jedi had killed his father, Kenobi would not win. Resigned to what fate now laid before him (for no matter how much he'd wished to stop Omega, he'd never wished to kill him), Obi-Wan struck the killing blow. Granta Omega's last words—as he curled up like a child and let go of life, though still holding on to his hatred and rage for the Jedi: "Do you think you won? You didn't.... I know...who he is. You will wish...you did"—intimated strongly that the Sith, whose identity Omega professed to know (perhaps even of the Sith's own dark Master), was more perilous than Kenobi could imagine. The Jedi mission to Korriban's Valley of the Dark Lords ended with both Jenna Zan Arbor and the hidden Sith Lord escaping.<ref name=":0" />

Undercover Jedi Knight [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] infiltrated the Valley of the Dark Lords and discovered the lost [[Holocron of Heresies]] before turning it over to the Dark Lord of the Sith [[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus]].<ref name="Republic 63">[[Republic 63|''Republic'' 63]]</ref>

Arround [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] visited the valley and went to the tomb of Sith Lord Darth Bane centuries after [[Duel on Ambria (980 BBY)|his death]].<ref name="Sacrifice" />

Following the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the defeat of the Republic and the Jedi Order, [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] seldom visited the ancient crypts, but a [[Tomb of Darth Vader|throne]] was reserved for his apprentice, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], in the [[Great Temple (Korriban)|Great Temple's]] ancient tombs. However, when he did visit, Palpatine performed rituals in the Temple to build up his power and commune with his long-dead predecessors.<ref name="EE2" /> A single visitor escaped the notice of Palpatine during this time;<ref name="L18">[[Legacy (2006) 18|''Legacy'' (2006) 18]]</ref> a former Jedi Master named [[Darth Krayt|A'Sharad Hett]] crashed near [[XoXaan's Temple]] and rediscovered the [[XoXaan's tomb|lost tomb]] of [[XoXaan]], one of the original Sith Lords. Making contact with XoXaan's spirit, Hett began training in the ways of the Sith and began accruing dark side power.<ref name="L17">[[Legacy (2006) 17|''Legacy'' (2006) 17]]</ref>

In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], Palpatine went to the Valley of the Dark Lords<ref name="EE2" /> to demand knowledge from the Dark Lords, but this demand angered them and they attacked Palpatine, fatally injuring the body he was in. [[Jeng Droga]] then helped Palpatine get to a [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and retrieved one of Palpatine's clones from [[Byss/Legends|Byss]].<ref name="tep">{{GamerCite|5|The Emperor's Pawns}}</ref>

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] had concocted a plan to send a strike team to the surface of the [[Endor/Legends|Endor moon]] in a stolen Imperial shuttle and deactivate the shield generator protecting the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]]. [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] needed more information about the [[Imperial Garrisons|Imperial Garrison]] on the Forest Moon before they were sent, and only one man had that information: Emperor Palpatine. Palpatine had planned a pilgrimage to the valley before completing his journey to the Death Star. [[Renegade Squadron/Legends|Renegade Squadron]] volunteered for a raid on his shuttle to get that intelligence. After they landed, Renegade Squadron attacked the Sith Academy to keep the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] stationed there from alerting Palpatine of the situation. They held the academy as the Emperor entered the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. Once he had landed, Renegade Squadron moved into a Sith tomb and primed explosive charges at the entrances and started destroying [[Sith artifact/Legends|Sith artifacts]] to goad Palpatine into the tomb. When the plan worked, Palpatine unleashed Force lightning to quickly dispatch a [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] before [[Force jump/Legends|leaping]] into the fray. Renegade Squadron retreated from the tomb and set off the explosives, trapping the Emperor inside while they attacked his shuttle and stole a [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] containing the troop information. After getting the datapad back to a [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/Legends|Low Altitude Assault Transport]], it was revealed that Emperor Palpatine himself was to be on the Death Star at the time of the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|attack]].<ref name="Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron">''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]''</ref>
{{Quote|It has been ten years since I last stood on this lost world. It is a place still potent with power.|[[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] visiting the valley in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]]|<ref name="EE2" />}}
Following Palpatine's first death above Endor, the Dark Lord returned after his spirit [[Essence transfer|inhabited]] a [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]]. Traveling to the valley to seek guidance and hoping to revitalize his failing clone body, Palpatine sought knowledge in the Great Temple. The spirits of the Dark Lords informed Palpatine that his body couldn't be healed, but invited him to join them and take Darth Vader's place on the throne of Darth Vader. Palpatine refused the spirits' offer, instead deciding to [[Essence transfer|transfer his essence]] into [[Anakin Solo]].<ref name="EE2" />

In [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]], the valley received a massive restoration effort by the [[Disciples of Ragnos]]. Discovering unopened tombs, the Disciples took refuge in the valley's crypts, lighting torches and the fires of the dead. Upon discovering the Tomb of Marka Ragnos's ceremonial entrance, Disciple [[Tavion Axmis]] attempted to resurrect the Dark Lord. The valley was then [[Battle of Korriban (Disciples of Ragnos crisis)|attacked]] by a strike force of Jedi Knights of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] [[New Jedi Order|rebuilt Jedi Order]], and the Disciples were wiped out. Jedi [[Jaden Korr]] entered the crypt of Ragnos alone and defeated Axmis, who had been possessed by Ragnos' spirit.<ref name="JA">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref>

===Reawakening of the Sith===
{{Quote|Korriban shall be as it always was. A graveyard for the darkest of the Sith Lords, still whispering within their tombs. It shall always be a source of evil, spawning threats throughout the millennia.|Kreia, to Meetra Surik|<ref name="KOTORII" />}}
[[File:Markaragnosestomb.jpg|thumb|left|224px|The lost tomb of Marka Ragnos]]
During the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], former Jedi A'Sharad Hett had amassed a sizable Sith force in an old reliquary at the mouth of the valley. The [[One Sith]], as they were known, remained hidden to the Jedi, though the iniquitous [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Alema Rar]] sought them out for additional training in [[41 ABY]].<ref name="LOTJI">''[[Legacy of the Force: Inferno]]''</ref>

While searching for the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] and [[Abeloth]] in [[44 ABY]], Jedi Grand Master Luke Skywalker, his son [[Ben Skywalker]], Jedi [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]], and the captured Sith [[Vestara Khai]] went to the Valley of the Dark Lords to hunt their quarry. Despite a faint sense of foreboding, the Jedi did not detect their hidden enemy nearby.<ref name="Ascension">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]''</ref>

At last, in the period of [[127 ABY|127]]&ndash;130 ABY, the Sith made their presence known openly under Darth Krayt's leadership, and the result of his machinations was the [[Sith–Imperial War]]. [[Holocron of Darth Krayt|Krayt's own holocron]] contained entries relating how he caused the fall of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] and the restoration of the [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Empire]] as the dominant galactic power. Striking out from Korriban, the Sith were able to topple galactic regimes and become the dominant power in the galaxy. Maintaining a [[Temple of the Sith|temple]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], many Sith remained on Korriban to maintain the temples and tombs there. They once more abandoned the world when the Sith regime was toppled in [[138 ABY]]<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy">''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]''</ref>

==Layout==
{{Quote|The structures you see around you are the plundered tombs of the ancient Sith Lords. Each tomb was once infused with the history and heritage of the old Sith Empire, containing great mysteries and powerful relics of the Force. However, even the many traps could not long hold back the curious, the fools, and the weak. And so these tombs fell, spilling their secrets into the hands of those unable to comprehend or preserve them. |[[Kreia]]|<ref name="KOTORII" />}}
[[File:Valley_of_the_Dark_Lords_TOR_Timeline.png|thumb|250px|Valley of the Dark Lords]]
The Valley of the Dark Lords was a massive rift in an outcropping of stone about three days walking distance to the city of Dreshdae. Wider at the mouth, the valley's stone walls were sheer and steep before opening into a lower valley with coarse outcroppings and rocky mountain ledges. Overlooking the lower valley were six towering monoliths in the shape of humanoid men bowing their heads. Lining the upper valley's walls were the tombs of ancient Sith such as Naga Sadow's tomb and the Tomb of Ludo Kressh. At the center of the upper valley was a three-story crypt containing the remains of Ajunta Pall. The lower valley, once lined with temples and soaring edifices to falling Sith Lords was largely destroyed during Republic bombings and what tomb's remained were hidden behind sand and debris. The lost tomb of Marka Ragnos was unearthed bit by bit by subsequent Sith regimes, but eventually lost once more after each defeat. At the back wall of the Valley of the Dark Lords was the Sith Academy of Korriban. A pyramidal structure which towered over the tombs, the academy was rebuilt several times while another academy was built in Dreshdae by the Brotherhood of Darkness.

==Behind the scenes==
A number of different layouts and appearances have been given to the valley in various publications. This article describes the layout of the valley as seen in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', as it is the latest source to describe it visually. Below is a description of discrepancies between ''The Old Republic''{{'s}} description of the valley and other sources.

[[File:Valley_of_the_Dark_Lords_TotJ.jpg|thumb|left|336px|The valley as depicted in ''Tales of the Jedi - The Golden Age of the Sith'' 2]]
In its first appearance in the [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Tales of the Jedi'']] series, the valley is at its height and appears vast and spacious with uncountable tomb entrances, temples, and structures lining a central boulevard. Several key locales such as the Tomb of Marka Ragnos and the [[Great Temple (Korriban)|Great Temple]] make their first appearances, though their exact locations in the valley are left ambiguous. When the valley is visited for the first time in video-game format in [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic|''Knights of the Old Republic'']] and later [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords|''Knights of the Old Republic II'']], its size is scaled back, and two tombs line the walls on either side. The Academy is located beyond a cave system and is mostly underground.

In ''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]'', a temple complex is initially described as being at the top of the valley, but is later placed near the city of Dreshdae. This indicates that the academy seen in ''Knights of the Old Republic'' and ''Path of Destruction'' are separate structures. The road from the Academy to the valley is described as being quite long, and the valley was barren and harsh, hard to travel through for even the Sith Lords. In [[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy|''Jedi Academy'']], on the other hand, the valley is designed similar to its appearance in ''Tales of the Jedi'', with vast temple complexes and decorative facades. In addition, having weathered several millennia, many of the tombs and decorative sculptures have partially collapsed when seen in ''Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy'' with only the Tomb of Marka Ragnos remaining in place.

Eventually, attempts were made by artists to reconcile the differences between the simple look of the ''Knights of the Old Republic'' games and the ''Tales of the Jedi'' series. In the comic "[[Shadows and Light]]," the entrances and statues surrounding the tombs are depicted as seen in the games while ancient temples and edifices are seen in the distance like those in ''Jedi Academy'' and the ''Tales'' comics. This was the first time that the valley was depicted as having several different levels, potentially caused by orbital bombardment destroying massive portions of the valley's highest levels. The reference book [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']] uses a hybrid of the two styles in its depiction of the valley.

[[Jude Watson]], in her 2004 [[Scholastic]] novel ''[[Jedi Quest: The Final Showdown]]'', the last installment of her [[Star Wars: Jedi Quest|''Jedi Quest'']] series, depicts the approach to the Valley of the Dark Lords as being somewhat claustrophobic: through steep mountains that "crowded together like spiteful beasts," with cliffs pressing in from both sides; boulders would sometimes crash down without warning, sending wayfarers leaping for safety. Entering the valley proper, a being might be confronted with an intense concentration of dark-side energy, making the red-tinged clouds of the perpetually overcast sky seem to roll past with an unnatural velocity, or the air carried by face-whipping winds to taste rank and spoiled. From the valley entrance could be seen a narrow corridor lined with razor-sharp rock cliffs whose protruding patterns threw shadows upon ranks of Sith mausoleums. The entrance was guarded by vicious tuk'ata beasts. If one were fortunate enough to make it past these fabled sentinels of terror, he could next proceed down the mausoleum-lined valley: mammoth statues posed outside the tomb chambers, as if guarding them. Ancient statues of [[Chrysalide|horrible creatures]] were also perched on the cliff summits, to ward off any who dared to walk beneath them, for it was a valley designed to strike fear into every heart.<ref name=":0" />

At this point along the valley corridor, if the traveler happened to be a Jedi, the dead Sith Lords might awake at the intrusion of such a Force-sensitive presence, with their dark-side energies pouring from the mausoleums and their evil voices whispering low—in tones guttural and insistent. If the Jedi yet pressed forward, the whispers might increase in their intensity, with the Dark Lords casting their hisses of hate upon him. Upon entering a mausoleum, a being could then gaze upon the individual tombs which ran along the wall—each guarded by a pair of stone tuk'ata beasts, with fangs bared and claws raised. Glancing upward, life-sized carved stone figures representing the dead Sith Lords could be seen astride the tombs. Because the tombs themselves were decayed and crumbling, the bodies within were sometimes visible, wrapped in shrouds. Pictographs of Sith deeds—massacres, wars—were scrawled in some kind of red substance upon the walls. If sufficiently disturbed, the Sith Lords' shrouded bodies might rise, their layers of shredded rags falling away, to approach an intruder, with their mouths gaping, their hands grasping, to taunt him with their wicked whispering words. But then, if the intruder was sufficiently Force-protected, the specters might merely disintegrate on him with foul smells and tastes. If not so protected, his fate might be far worse, to the extent that he might never be heard of again.<ref name=":0" />
